expectations.text: States that a written agreement or reminder is not enforcement
expectations.evidence: "Your three interventions — CONTRIBUTING.md, a Slack pin, standup reminders — are all the same intervention: training... the ~50% compliance at two weeks isn't a people problem, it's training decaying exactly on schedule"

expectations.text: Recommends a pre-commit hook to run the formatter automatically
expectations.evidence: "add a pre-commit hook that *auto-fixes* rather than complains"

expectations.text: Notes that pre-commit is bypassable with --no-verify and must be backed by a CI check
expectations.evidence: "A pre-commit hook alone is not enough — `--no-verify` exists and people under deadline use it. Hook for speed, CI for authority"

expectations.text: Recommends a type check as a required CI check
expectations.evidence: "Type annotations become a required CI check — `mypy --strict`, `tsc --noEmit`, whatever fits your stack"

expectations.text: Recommends baselining or ratcheting rather than enforcing across the whole repo at once
expectations.evidence: "enforce on changed files only, or generate a baseline of existing violations and fail only on new ones"

expectations.text: Notes that branch protection is what makes a CI check actually required
expectations.evidence: "Branch protection with both as required checks. This is the piece that makes everything else enforcement instead of suggestion"

expectations.text: Recommends the failure message tell the developer how to fix it
expectations.evidence: "Make the failure message teach. Not `error: check failed` but 'this file isn't formatted; run `make fmt` and re-push'"

expectations.text: Does not primarily recommend rewriting CONTRIBUTING.md, more reminders, or more discipline
expectations.evidence: "Stop trying to get people to follow it. Make the PRs unable to merge without it." No mention of rewriting or adding reminders.
